text:
ben_customer: Hey team — noticed a compliance issue. Our org default retention is 30d but some objects older than 35-40d are still returning in search. Need urgent confirmation these were actually deleted.

emma_support: Sorry to hear that, Ben. Can you share the account/org id and a couple of example object IDs or request IDs so we can look up logs? Also, did you recently change any retention settings?

ben_customer: account: org_7782, sample object IDs: obj_2024_00987, obj_2024_01022. No retention changes on our side; app uses default. We call delete via DELETE /v1/objects/{id} then rely on TTL.

emma_support: Thanks. Pulling logs now. One quick repro check: do you see the tombstone flag on the object metadata when fetched with the internal debug api? e.g., GET /internal/objects/{id}?show_meta=true

ben_customer: ran that, still returns {
  "id": "obj_2024_00987",
  "state": "available",
  "deleted_at": "2024-01-05T12:03:22Z"
} — deleted_at present but object still searchable.

emma_support: Hmm. That suggests tombstone set but index not updated or object still in read path. Escalating to infra/SRE. @raj_eng can you take a look?

raj_eng: On it. Initial hypothesis: two possibilities — 1) retention policy override at org or tenant policy level preserving beyond default, 2) indexer failures after KMS rotation prevented tombstone propagation to search index. Pulling indexer logs for org_7782 now.

retention-bot: Note: There is a cross-org policy override in effect for org_7782 — preserve=true, min_retention_days=90. Set by config push 2024-01-02T03:12:00Z by ops:lisa_ops.

lisa_ops: Confirming I rolled out a temporary preserve override for a subset of customers during a migration window (we should have excluded org_7782, will investigate). It was meant to apply to billing-migration-flagged orgs only.

ben_customer: That explains why objects are still visible. But we never got notice. What's the rollback plan? Legal needs confirmation for compliance.

sarah_legal: We need to treat this as an incident for external communications. If an org's objects were preserved beyond their advertised TTL without consent we should prepare a disclosure and remediation timeline. Please provide an exact list of affected object IDs and whether any exports were done.

miguel_sre: Indexer logs show repeated errors starting 2024-01-04 22:10 UTC: 

```
2024-01-04T22:10:07Z indexer[org_7782] WARN: KMS: Decrypt failed for reindex job: AccessDenied
2024-01-04T22:10:07Z indexer[org_7782] ERROR: tombstone propagation failed for obj_2024_00987, retrying
2024-01-04T22:10:07Z indexer[org_7782] ERROR: max retries reached, marking backlog
```

miguel_sre: Those errors line up with a KMS key rotation that changed the key version used by the indexer role. The storage layer shows deleted_at set, but the indexer couldn't update the search index because it couldn't decrypt metadata for reprocessing.

raj_eng: So root cause is twofold: 1) an unintended preserve override applied to the org, and 2) KMS rotation blocking the indexer from completing tombstone propagation. The override kept objects available even though deletion timestamps existed.

emma_support: Actionable next steps I propose: 
- ops (lisa_ops) to rollback the preserve override for org_7782 (immediate).
- SRE (miguel_sre) to run an authenticated reindex job once KMS permissions confirmed.
- Eng (raj_eng) to produce a precise export of affected object IDs and whether any read/export activity happened while preserved.
- Legal (sarah_legal) to draft customer communication and retention disclosure.

lisa_ops: Rolling back override now. ETA ~15m. Will post confirmation.

miguel_sre: I'll coordinate with infra-kms to re-grant indexer decrypt after rollback. Once permissions fixed, I'll run the backlog reindex which will propagate tombstones and remove items from search. Reindex job steps (for records):
```
1) validate KMS key version
2) run re-encrypt/re-decrypt step with indexer identity
3) replay tombstone updates to search index
4) verify search does not return deleted objects for random sample
```

ben_customer: What's the estimated time to fully purge from search? We need this for compliance reporting.

miguel_sre: If rollback + KMS fix go smoothly, reindex should process backlog in ~4 hours for this org. I'll update if re-encryption throttles.

raj_eng: For customers who need immediate removal, we can run an emergency purge on the search index for the provided object IDs as a stop-gap. That will remove visibility even before reindex completes. Requires ops approval.

emma_support: Ben — would you like an emergency purge for the sample IDs while we fix the root cause?

ben_customer: Yes please, run purge for the sample set and any others you find in export. Also please include a signed statement of what happened and timeline.

sarah_legal: We'll prepare the formal statement once Eng provides the full affected list and timeline. Keep all logs and change records.

lisa_ops: Override rollback complete at 2024-01-05T01:22:10Z. Confirmed no further applies to org_7782.

miguel_sre: KMS permissions corrected, indexer can decrypt now. Starting reindex backlog run. Starting with sample batch of 500 objects, will escalate to full backlog on success.

retention-bot: Backlog job queued: job_5532, priority=high, objects_estimate=12k.

miguel_sre: Sample batch cleared and search verification passed for sample IDs. Scheduling full backlog, ETA ~3.5 hours.

emma_support: Noted. Actions: emergency purge executed for the sample IDs, override rollback confirmed, reindex in progress. Will follow up with export + timeline doc for legal. Ben — we'll update you in ~4 hours or sooner.

ben_customer: Thanks all. Please include the exact list exported and whether any external exports/downloads occurred while preserve=true. Critical for audit.

raj_eng: Understood — compiling exports/logs now. Will add a CSV with object_id, deleted_at, preserve_flag, search_visible_since to the ticket.

sarah_legal: Also attach IAM change logs showing the override rollout and who approved it.

emma_support: Closing interim update — next message will contain the full remediation timeline and artifacts.

#end of thread
